newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips on commercial demand for dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips on commercial demand for dlrs.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed a shade lower against the dollar on Thursday due to higher commercial demand for the greenback, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.40 to the dollar after opening at 58.35 and falling to 58.43, they said.
"The rupee fell to 58.43 on import covering," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
Despite overseas gains by the dollar, the Central Bank has remained lukewarm towards the currency, keeping speculators away, dealers said.
The Central Bank left the dollar-rupee exchange rate unchanged at 58.3259 and 59.5042.
"We do not expect to see much movement in the exchange rate on Friday if the Central Bank is not positive towards the dollar," the HongKong Bank dealer said.
Overnight call money closed at nine percent, after opening at 14, dealers said.
"The market was so very well offered that banks ended up at the Central Bank's repurchase rate of nine percent," said an American Express Bank dealer.
